mechanism_narrative: RETAIL_REC has risen in each of the last three weeks, and this autoregressive recovery momentum will persist as restrictions loosen, causing the next 28-day mean to exceed the prior 28-day mean.
failure_condition: The mean of RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days is less than or equal to its mean over the last 28 days despite three consecutive weekly increases.

mechanism_narrative: Transit station mobility leads retail footfall because commuting and discretionary trips use the same network; continued TRANSIT improvement above 2 points per week will pull RETAIL_REC higher over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT rises by more than 2.0 points week-on-week for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: After TRANSIT logs two consecutive weekly gains above 2.0 points, the next 14-day mean of RETAIL_REC is not higher than its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Simultaneous gains in PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM reduce perceived infection risk and normalize out-of-home routines, jointly lifting RETAIL_REC over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both improve by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: When PARKS and GROCERY_PHARM both rise, RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days fails to exceed its prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Falling RESIDENTIAL mobility means fewer people are staying home, increasing out-of-home retail exposure; each weekly drop in RESIDENTIAL predicts higher RETAIL_REC next week.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 0.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: A weekly RESIDENTIAL decline greater than 0.5 points is followed by a 7-day RETAIL_REC mean that is not higher than the preceding 7-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Continued recovery in WORKPLACES mobility indicates more commuting and daytime population, which raises weekday retail and recreation visits over four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises for four consecutive weeks, yet the next 28-day mean of RETAIL_REC is lower than its last 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A relaxation of stay-at-home policy is revealed by joint increases in TRANSIT and WORKPLACES; this policy regime will continue to lift RETAIL_REC over four weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and WORKPLACES both improve by more than 1.5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: In weeks when both TRANSIT and WORKPLACES improve by >1.5 points, the next 28-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 28-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: Seasonal spring weather raises PARKS mobility, and greater park activity spills over into nearby retail corridors, lifting RETAIL_REC over two weeks.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 8 points over two weeks
failure_condition: After PARKS improves by more than 8 points over two weeks, the next 14-day RETAIL_REC mean is not higher than the prior 14-day mean.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp PARKS rebound while GROCERY_PHARM stays depressed signals people socializing outdoors but avoiding enclosed retail, which diverts trips and lowers RETAIL_REC next week.
candidate_trigger: PARKS improves by more than 10 points over two weeks while GROCERY_PHARM remains below -35
failure_condition: Under the trigger, the next 7-day mean of RETAIL_REC is equal to or higher than the prior 7-day mean.
